blocks.content: Inbound SCIM provisioning is a realm-level feature. Click the button below to confirm your realm administrator has enabled it. If not, ask the admin to enable SCIM in the organizations configuration.
Sign in to the Okta admin console.
In the left navigation, expand the Applications section and select the Applications tab. Click Browse App Catalog.

blocks.alt: Okta Applications page with Browse App Catalog button highlighted

blocks.content: Search for SCIM 2.0 Test App (OAuth Bearer Token) and select the matching result.

blocks.alt: Okta Browse App Integration Catalog with search results for SCIM 2.0 Test App

blocks.content: On the page that opens, click Add Integration.

blocks.alt: SCIM 2.0 Test App detail page with Add Integration button

blocks.content: Give the application a descriptive name (for example, the name of the realm being provisioned). Click Next.

blocks.alt: Add SCIM 2.0 Test App General settings — Application label field

blocks.content: You can leave the Sign-On Options at their defaults. Click Done.

blocks.alt: Sign-On Options page with Done button

blocks.content: Click the button below. The wizard generates a high-entropy OAuth Bearer Token and writes the SCIM configuration to this organization. The token is shown on the next step — copy it before leaving.
In your Okta SCIM application, go to the Provisioning tab and click Configure API Integration.

blocks.alt: Provisioning tab showing 'Provisioning is not enabled' with Configure API Integration button

blocks.content: Check Enable API Integration. Paste the values below into the SCIM 2.0 Base URL and OAuth Bearer Token fields.

blocks.alt: Enable API Integration form with SCIM 2.0 Base URL and OAuth Bearer Token fields

blocks.label: SCIM 2.0 Base URL
blocks.hint: Paste into the SCIM 2.0 Base URL field

blocks.label: OAuth Bearer Token
blocks.warning: Copy this value now — it cannot be recovered later. Anyone holding it can push users and groups into this organization.
blocks.hint: Paste into the OAuth Bearer Token field

blocks.content: Click Test API Credentials in Okta to verify the connection, then click Save.
On the Provisioning tab, click To App in the left navigation. You will see Create Users, Update User Attributes, and Deactivate Users are disabled by default.

blocks.alt: Provisioning To App tab showing default disabled state

blocks.content: Click Edit, check Enable next to Create Users, Update User Attributes, and Deactivate Users, then click Save.

blocks.alt: Provisioning actions enabled with checkboxes ticked and Save button

blocks.content: Optional: review the attribute mappings under Test SCIM App Attribute Mappings. The defaults work for most realms; you can return here later to add custom mappings.

blocks.alt: Test SCIM App Attribute Mappings page showing default Okta to SCIM attribute mappings

blocks.content: In the Okta application, go to the Assignments tab. Click Assign and select Assign to People.

blocks.alt: Assignments tab with the Assign dropdown showing 'Assign to People' option

blocks.content: In the dialog that opens, search for and assign each user who should be provisioned, then click Done.

blocks.alt: Assign Test SCIM App to People dialog with a user selected and Done button

blocks.content: For each user, review the profile fields that will be sent over SCIM. Most fields can be left blank — Okta will sync the default profile attributes. Click Save and Go Back.

blocks.alt: User assignment form with Save and Go Back button

blocks.content: Now go to the Push Groups tab. Click Push Groups and select Find groups by name. Locate the appropriate group, enable Push group memberships immediately, and click Save. Okta will start pushing users and groups within a few minutes.

blocks.alt: Push Groups by name dialog with a group selected and Save button

blocks.title: SCIM provisioning is configured
blocks.description: Okta will start pushing users and groups within a few minutes. Sync events appear in the Keycloak admin console under Events.
